Advance the three enabled voice streams through $0813/$0B61/$0CFF, then update pitch sequences, pulse widths and the shared filter sweep. The index X runs from 2 to 0. The pulse-update test reads the three instruction bytes at $0B27,X; these are nonzero in this image. $0A0F is rewritten to choose the voice arpeggio pointer.
Return in A the OR of the three voice-enable bytes $20AC–$20AE. Zero means every stream has processed its stop command; SID envelopes can still decay after that.

Advance voice 1, stream pointer $84/$85. A duration countdown delays fetching the next item; when a second countdown $2046 expires it can write $2073 to $D404 (flag bit 0). Values below $80 select pitch indices, with $5E skipping the new pitch; values $80–$97 dispatch through the split command table. Fixed duration consumes one note byte; explicit duration consumes note and duration. Note flags in $20B2 gate the pulse (bit 1) and filter (bit 2) resets and the gate write (bit 0); vibrato is reset whenever vibrato is enabled. Common frequency output follows through $0947; voice 3 also writes its saved sustain/release bytes to $D414 at each fetch.
Low operand byte of the self-modified JMP at $0944. Voice 1 command dispatch replaces this from $1439 plus command index.

For voice X, leave frequency to the arpeggio sequencer when $2070,X is set. Otherwise apply enabled vibrato and write the base low/high pitch bytes through $0AFD.

For voice X, wait the initial delay, then alternately add and subtract the low-byte step $205E,X to the 16-bit base frequency $2037,X/$203A,X. The phase length comes from $2058,X, and the phase flag flips when its counter reaches zero.

For voice X, decrement its step timer. On zero, reload it and read a pitch offset through the pointer selected by the self-modified operand at $0A0F. Add the current note index, look up the resulting SID frequency at $1529/$1588, and write its two bytes. Advance the sequence index, wrapping to 2 at the stored end.

Zero-page operand of LDA (pointer),Y at $0A0E. The tick starts it at $8E for voice 3 and decrements it twice for each next voice, selecting $8C and $8A. Y is that voice's sequence offset; the following code adds the base note and writes the looked-up SID frequency.

For voice X, add or subtract $207F,X from the 16-bit pulse-width work value $208E,X/$2094,X, and write the SID pulse registers. Separate countdowns and reloads select rising and falling phases; eight-bit counter underflow follows the processor arithmetic.

Advance the shared filter cutoff up or down using low/high step bytes $20A4/$20A5. OR $F8 into the low byte before writing $D415 and write the high byte to $D416. Two countdowns alternate the direction and reload their phase lengths.

Publish shared enemy lane Y for four sprite components. For slot X copy raw X to its two components; when display flags, expanded-component state and facing require it, place the second component 24 raw units to the left with borrow.

Sixteen return-address-minus-one words indexed by the active-high direction nibble. Valid up/down/left/right combinations choose jump, duck or facing-dependent attacks; neutral and contradictory combinations select return $A055.
Return immediately. Directional-fire table entries for neutral and contradictory direction combinations point here.
Four byte offsets indexed by facing/action: $04,$F2,$0C,$F0. Hit tests add these with native byte wrapping before comparing enemy half-X.
Decrement enemy slot X and loop to the type-4 hit test while nonnegative; otherwise return.
Visit slots 1 then 0, requiring type 4 and a narrow facing-indexed half-X/lane window. A match sets pose and hit state to $AB. Player action flags select this path through $968C.
Nine type-indexed hurt-pose starts used by $A0F9 when health differs from one.
Nine type-indexed settlement-pose starts used by $A0F9 when health equals one, including the path that first restores underflowed health to one.
Decrement enemy slot X and continue the ordinary player-hit test at $A0B9 while nonnegative.
Ten retained score bytes indexed by enemy type. $A0F9 adds the selected value as low packed BCD in units of 100 displayed points; active type values select their corresponding awards.

Visit enemy slots 1 then 0. Skip an existing hit state; type 6 additionally requires remembered direction bit 1. Test a facing-indexed horizontal window and four-unit lane band. On a hit, use type score byte $A0AD,Y and continue through $A0F9.

Store score amount A in pending low BCD, add it through $FC5A, and request effect 11. Choose a type-dependent hurt or settlement pose from $A097/$A0A0 according to health. Set forced horizontal step +1. If facing left, turn right and update component mirrors, then start the jump at $A31A.
Set forced horizontal step -1. If facing right, turn left and update component mirrors, then enter the jump setup.

Compare horizontal direction with facing. The matching direction requests effect 10 and starts pose $16 (restart $14) with a five-count delay, unless a hold is active ($0648 nonzero), when it returns without acting. The opposite direction enters $A21C, which handles holds by enemy type and hold counter.
For enemy slot Y, subtract one from $0672,Y. Store and return while nonnegative; underflow enters hold release at $A1E0.
Set enemy reaction pose $48 with restart $3E, clear shared and per-slot grab flags, and start player hurt pose $28/hit lock. Reset timing, face opposite the enemy and select the HUD pulse reaction.

During a hold, type 8 joins the hold-counter path; other types lose one health and enter a reaction pose before the hold clears. Set player pose $1D and restart $14, delay ten and action state. X=$1D remains live at the indexed store $A268, so that store writes $FF to $06AC, not to an enemy cadence slot.

Select front or back attack by comparing horizontal input with facing. A front attack uses pose $0D, or $07 when object state 2 means the player holds the weapon; both use delay five. The opposite direction starts pose $24 with delay fifteen. Request the corresponding sound and set action state.

Set repeat marker $FF and player pose $14. If object state is 3, require its Y in the tested eight-unit band and player half-X in the tested sixteen-unit band; a match makes it player-held state 2. Clear pose delay and select the crouch frame.
Set current/restart pose $21, active action and jump phase 1, clear pose delay and select the initial sprite frame through $9635.
Read joystick port 1 at $DC01, invert its five low bits, and store active-high up/down/left/right/fire bits in $0611. Keyboard bits above bit 4 are discarded.
Store A in $0612 and return; this is the zero-direction exit of the fire-held direction handler.

With fire held, isolate the direction nibble. A zero nibble is only remembered. When $0648 is nonzero, accept down plus a horizontal direction before continuing. On a changed direction, store the raw nibble and RTS-dispatch through target-minus-one words at $A035. Unchanged input instead follows the signed horizontal override in $0615 through $A37A.
Store A into remembered direction $0612 and reset the player pose through $9624, then continue forced horizontal movement handling at $A37A.

If $0615 is nonzero, synthesize left ($04) for a negative byte or right ($08) for a positive byte; otherwise clear directional input. Store this in $0611 and continue at the horizontal part of player movement, $A3E8.

Compute the low byte of the player's 16-bit X position divided by two in $062C. Active $0613 or $0647 state redirects through the forced-horizontal path. Fire-held input goes to the directional attack dispatcher. Without fire, set the remembered attack direction to $FF; $0648 also forces horizontal processing. Up decrements floor Y while it is at least $74, so it stops at $73 (no limit when $0676 is nonzero); down stops at $A4, and the floor value becomes draw Y. Left/right update facing and $067C ($12/$10). Depending on camera phase, screen-X bounds, stage limits and $067E, move the player's 16-bit X by one or request camera motion in $0652 while stepping fine-scroll $17. Wrapping fine scroll sets the coarse-scroll request $0600. The coordinate and camera branches share the return at $A4D6.

Input X selects an enemy's horizontal position at $064C,X/$064E,X and direction bits at $0664,X. Unless $0635 is nonzero, bit 0 decrements the shared Y byte $064B while it is at least $74 (stopping at $73) and bit 1 increments it below $AD. Bit 2 decrements the selected X position after a divided-position lower-bound check ($0E), except that when bit 1 is set and $064B is already $AD the code branches past the bit-2 step; bit 3 increments it. Apply signed camera motion $0652 to the selected X afterward, including carry/borrow into its high byte. The Y loads and stores here are deliberately recorded as unindexed, as the bytes implement them.

Tail entry into the shared enemy movement routine: with slot X retained, apply signed camera correction $0652 to its raw horizontal coordinate. The ordinary AI cadence uses this without performing a fresh direction step.

Move colour rows 1–19 upward by one row across all 40 columns, covering $D800–$DAF7 as destinations. Clear coarse-scroll request $0600, toggle screen-buffer bit $10 in $0609, increment $0209, and jump to $AF3D to prepare the next display data. Called from the vertical-scroll transition at $836A.

Select the direction with $0679. Zero shifts each of 20 colour rows left by one cell (columns 1–39 to 0–38), clears $0600, toggles screen-buffer bit $10 in $0609, increments the 16-bit camera offset $0207/$0208, and draws through $2A67. Nonzero enters $A6A9 for the opposite shift. The zero path clears $0676 before returning.

Shift columns 0–38 to 1–39 in colour rows 1–19, leaving row zero unchanged. Iterate backward to preserve source cells. Clear $0600, toggle $0609 bit $10, decrement camera offset $0207/$0208, and jump to left-edge redraw $2A3C.

Six stage-indexed music cue numbers 1,3,1,2,3,8. The five playable stages use the first five; ending setup subsequently starts cue 4.

Visit swap flags 5 down through 0. For each nonzero flag call $84FE with its slot to exchange the resource back, then explicitly clear the flag.
